labels.firstRun.title: Welcome to WPods

labels.firstRun.trayDesc: Closing the window keeps WPods running.

labels.legal.firstRunBody: WPods is an independent, open-source project. It isn't made, sponsored, endorsed or supported by Apple. AirPods and the names of their features belong to Apple Inc.; WPods uses them only to say what it works with. WPods comes with no warranty: you use it, including its drivers, at your own risk. To load its drivers, WPods also turns on Windows test mode (test signing), which needs Secure Boot off and a restart; see the full terms.
labels.legal.testModeBody: WPods installs its own kernel drivers, test-signed by the project and not signed by Microsoft. To load them, Setup turns on Windows test signing (test mode), which needs Secure Boot off and a restart. While test mode is on, Windows will load any test-signed kernel driver, not only WPods', so a Windows security protection stays lowered until you turn it off. Windows shows a "Test Mode" watermark on the desktop while test mode is on; WPods does not add or remove it, but a separate open-source tool to hide it is available at https://github.com/FPNDev/no-test-mode-wm (use it at your own risk). This is reversible: uninstalling WPods, or running bcdedit /set testsigning off as an administrator, turns it back off.

labels.pair.step3Desc: WPods finds them on its own after that.
labels.home.hintBuds: Open the case near your PC, or put your AirPods in your ears.
labels.home.hintMax: Take your AirPods Max out of the Smart Case to wake them.
labels.home.hintElsewhere: Connecting here takes them over from the other device.
labels.home.keysHint: Connect once to enable nearby detection.
labels.home.controlsDesc: Noise modes, press speed, tone volume
labels.nc.title: Noise control
labels.nc.oneBudNote: Noise Cancellation needs both AirPods in, or turn on "Noise cancellation with one AirPod".
labels.nc.outOfEarNote: Put an AirPod in your ear to change noise control.
labels.mic.title: Microphone
labels.mic.desc.notActive: Apps can use your AirPods as the microphone "Headset (A2DP)".
labels.mic.desc.live: An app is using your AirPods microphone.
labels.mic.desc.problem: The microphone isn't coming through. Try reconnecting your AirPods.
labels.mic.note: Not Apple's processing: WPods runs public models locally under these names. Pick them in Windows settings > Mic modes.
labels.mic.modesDesc: Which modes show up and the model each one uses
labels.mic.modesGroupDesc: Modes you turn off disappear from the Home page. Keep at least one.
labels.mic.rawDesc: No model, no processing: the mic exactly as it comes in.
labels.mic.usageThreads: {threads} threads · ~{pct}% of one core · {delay} ms delay
labels.features.title: Features
labels.features.earDesc: Pauses audio when you take an AirPod out.
labels.features.earDescMax: Pauses audio when you take them off.
labels.features.conversationDesc: Lowers media and brings voices forward when you speak.
labels.features.duckDesc: How low media goes while you're talking.
labels.features.oneBudDesc: Keeps Noise Cancellation on with a single AirPod in.
labels.features.personalizedVolumeDesc: Adjusts media volume to your surroundings.
labels.features.allowOffDesc: Adds Off to the modes you cycle through by pressing the stem.
labels.features.allowOffDescMax: Adds Off to the modes you cycle through with the noise control button.
labels.features.heartRateDesc: Reads your pulse from the sensors in your AirPods.
labels.features.hearingAidDesc: Uses the hearing settings from your iPhone or iPad.
labels.features.hearingAidSetup: Set up Hearing Aid on your iPhone or iPad first.
labels.hr.note: AirPods aren't a medical device. Don't use these readings to diagnose or treat any condition.
labels.controls.title: Controls
labels.stem.title: Press and hold cycles through
labels.controls.pressSpeedDesc: How quickly you need to press twice.
labels.controls.holdDurationDesc: How long to hold before noise control changes.
labels.controls.toneDesc: The chimes your AirPods play, like the connect sound.

labels.windows.handsFreeDesc: Keeps audio in stereo. The microphone comes through WPods.
labels.windows.latencyDesc: Less delay for games and video calls.
labels.windows.latencyNote: Keeps your AirPods awake, so they may use more battery.
labels.windows.startupDesc: Opens in the tray when you sign in.
labels.windows.themeDesc: Auto follows your Windows app mode.
labels.windows.accentDesc: Matches the colour you chose in Personalisation.

labels.toast.noResponse: Your AirPods didn't respond. Try reconnecting.
labels.toast.connectFailed: Couldn't connect. Make sure the case is open and nearby.
labels.toast.micFailed: Something went wrong with the microphone (error {code}). Try reconnecting your AirPods.
labels.toast.lowLatencyFailed: Low audio latency couldn't start. Make sure your AirPods are the output device.
labels.toast.handsFreeFailed: Couldn't change Hands-Free mode. Try again.
labels.toast.micModelFailed: This model couldn't load (error {code}). WPods keeps using the previous one.
labels.toast.micModeStopped: A microphone mode stopped working and was turned off (error {code}). Reconnect your AirPods to try again.
labels.toast.settingsReset: Your settings couldn't be read, so WPods started with default settings (error {code}).
labels.toast.webviewFailed: WPods couldn't open its window. Make sure Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime is installed (error {code}).
